title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
sourceTitle: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
synopsis: A broken fellowship, a creature in the marshes, and ten thousand Uruks at the gate of an old fortress.

nodes.text: A wet, gray maze of stones, and footsteps not your own behind you. Both choices lead to Smeagol's Bargain, but “Set a trap” arrives there with a different cost than “Press on.” By Smeagol's Bargain, hesitation will have spent time you cannot recover.

choices.consequence: You choose to set a trap. By Smeagol's Bargain, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.
You choose to press on. By Smeagol's Bargain, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: He swears on the precious to be your guide. Both choices lead to The Three Hunters, but “Bind him” arrives there with a different cost than “Believe him.” At The Three Hunters, everyone involved will know which risk you accepted.

choices.consequence: You bind him. The route to The Three Hunters opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.
You believe him. The route to The Three Hunters opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Aragorn presses his ear to the ground. Two days ahead, maybe more. Riders of Rohan is already waiting. What changes is whether “Run” or “Rest first” is the instinct you carry into it. In The Three Hunters, the safer route is disappearing faster than the danger.

choices.consequence: You run. The route to Riders of Rohan opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.
You choose to rest first. By Riders of Rohan, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: A line of horsemen breaks over the ridge with spears down. Fangorn's Edge will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Stand and speak” than after “Hide in the grass.”

choices.consequence: You stand and speak. The route to Fangorn's Edge opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.
You hide in the grass. The route to Fangorn's Edge opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: A forest that watches you back, breathing slowly. The road still runs toward Treebeard. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Enter” and choosing “Skirt it.” By Treebeard, hesitation will have spent time you cannot recover.

choices.consequence: You commit to enter. It buys momentum toward Treebeard and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.
You choose to skirt it. By Treebeard, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

You speak slow. The route to Edoras opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Ambush on the plain, and Aragorn over the cliff. Glittering Caves comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Chase the wargs” and “Get the people inside.” In Warg Riders, the safer route is disappearing faster than the danger.

nodes.text: There's some good in this world, and it's worth fighting for. The paths divide here: “Believe it” leads into The Hall Holds, while “Walk on quietly” makes Dawn Charge the next reckoning. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Carrying the Carrier in play.

choices.consequence: You believe it. The route to The Hall Holds opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.
You choose to walk on quietly. By Dawn Charge, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You choose to take the third path. By Carrying the Carrier, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: The hornblast at dawn is yours. You hold the keep until white riders break the line, and you sleep that night in a cold corner that feels like home. The road into The Hall Holds began with “Believe it” in Sam's Speech; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
You ride with Aragorn out of the gate and into a song the Mark will sing for a thousand years. Half of you comes back. All of it matters. You are unlikely to keep all three.

Frodo cannot, so you do. Up a long road that has no name yet, you carry the man who carries the ring, and nobody writes that part down for centuries. The road into Carrying the Carrier began with “Take the third path” in Sam's Speech; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
